profiles.name: Chablis Grand Cru

terroir.geography: single delimited slope on the right bank of the Serein near Chablis

styleNotes: dry, vivid and fruit-driven Chardonnay with notable minerality
can be austere young and gain complexity and finesse with age
INAO describes approximately ten years as a typical point of plenitude rather than a legal drinking window

profiles.name: Gevrey-Chambertin
styleNotes: ruby red with intense small-fruit aromas
powerful, densely tannic yet capable of velvety texture
grand cru wines are associated with spice, violet and forest-floor development and substantial longevity
researchNotes: The nine named grands crus are separate AOPs, not simply a 'grand cru tier' inside the Gevrey-Chambertin AOP. Generation must preserve that legal distinction.

profiles.name: Meursault

terroir.geography: appellation area confined to the commune of Meursault on the Côte de Beaune

styleNotes: white wines are dry, concentrated and persistent
toasted and almond-like aromatic notes are common descriptors in the official product presentation
acidity supports ageing
researchNotes: Red Meursault exists but is exceptional. The game should not force every Meursault bottle to white, but white must dominate generation weights.
The exact 19 premier-cru climats will be entered only from the current specification or official climate list.

profiles.name: Aloxe-Corton
styleNotes: red wines are structured and tannic with red- and black-fruit aromas
white wines show mineral character and fresh white-fruit aromas
researchNotes: Corton, Corton-Charlemagne and Charlemagne are separate grand-cru AOPs related geographically to the hill, not internal labels that can be freely appended to Aloxe-Corton.

profiles.name: Margaux

terroir.climate: mild winters, good sunshine and generally moderate summer drought; forest to the west reduces ocean-wind exposure

styleNotes: ageworthy structured reds noted for aromatic richness and finesse
Cabernet Sauvignon contributes cassis, green-pepper and cedar descriptors; Merlot red/black plum-fruit; Cabernet Franc floral red fruit; Petit Verdot blueberry/coffee descriptors

profiles.name: Pomerol

terroir.geography: Pomerol commune and part of Libourne; relatively flat terraces shaped by Isle deposits

styleNotes: Merlot is dominant and contributes dense color, black fruit, violet and truffle-like development
Cabernet varieties and Côt/Malbec contribute structure and complexity
wines can support long bottle ageing
researchNotes: Pomerol has no official classified-growth hierarchy. The game must not fabricate a 'Grand Cru Classé' tier for Pomerol.

profiles.name: Sauternes

productionRules.botrytisRole: noble rot concentrates berries and sugar

terroir.climateMechanism: night humidity, particularly from the Ciron/Garonne system, alternating with fine autumn days supports Botrytis cinerea

styleNotes: young wines show floral and fruit aromas
ageing develops candied fruit, citrus and honey descriptors with long aromatic persistence
researchNotes: Exact current grape percentages, minimum potential alcohol/sugar and yield rules remain to be extracted from the March 2026 specification before blend generation is fully strict.

profiles.name: Saint-Émilion
styleNotes: Merlot is the dominant variety and contributes roundness and red/black fruit
Cabernet Franc contributes freshness, finesse and firmer tannin
Cabernet Sauvignon contributes spice and power
researchNotes: Saint-Émilion and Saint-Émilion Grand Cru are separate appellations. The word 'grand cru' is therefore not a generic quality adjective in the generator.

profiles.name: Saint-Émilion Grand Cru
styleNotes: lower-yield and longer-ageing requirements distinguish grand-cru production from the base Saint-Émilion appellation
barrel maturation is common and supports ageing potential
researchNotes: The classified-growth list is periodically revised. It must be versioned by classification cycle rather than treated as timeless metadata.
Producer classification is a separate axis from the appellation itself.

profiles.name: Barbaresco
researchNotes: MASAF published a consolidated Barbaresco DOCG production specification on 4 March 2026.

The legacy project already contains extensive Barbaresco MGA material. That material will remain reference-only until the 2026 specification is extracted field by field for grape composition, ageing, release and MGA/vigna naming rules.
